Sam (customer-success): FYI ACME says their quantized endpoint is slower than FP16 and outputs degraded. They opened a support ticket with a few request IDs and some transcripts. https://redwood.logs/req/abc123 :grimacing:

Priya (eng-runtime): thanks — can you paste the endpoint name, model alias, and a p95 comparison? any recent deploys?

Sam (customer-success): endpoint: acme-prod-gen
model alias: redwood/open-oz-7b-q4k-v2 (4-bit kernel auto)
traffic: ~100 rps steady
FP16 (before) p95 = 180ms, CPU/GPU p50 ~70ms
Quant (after) p95 = 420ms, p50 ~200ms
recent deploy: quant rollout yesterday ~17:05 UTC
sample prompt: `Summarize the product launch in two sentences for a blog audience.`

Marta (eng-ml): that p95 jump + higher error rate matches a calibration/caching problem we've seen. Can you grep the logs for "calibration applied" and "kv-cache-miss" and paste a short snippet? Also include one request-id where p95 was high.

Sam (customer-success): pasted small log snippet below (sanitized):

```
[2026-11-04T17:07:22Z] req=abc123 stage=decode kernel=q4k-v2 status=start
[2026-11-04T17:07:22Z] req=abc123 stage=decoding calibration=applied latency_ms=32
[2026-11-04T17:07:22Z] req=abc123 kv-cache-miss=true cache_key=seq-42
[2026-11-04T17:07:22Z] req=abc123 stage=token-gen latency_ms=150 p95_deadline_miss=true
[2026-11-04T17:07:22Z] req=abc123 stage=decode kernel=fp16-fallback status=used_kv_cache
```

Sam (customer-success): also customer attached a short transcript showing more hallucinations on quantized path.

Priya (eng-runtime): quick triage notes: if calibration is being applied per-request (instead of using a calibration cache keyed by model+quant-params+cache-version) we see extra CPU/GPU prep cost and KV cache churn. That explains both latency and quality changes.

Marta (eng-ml): +1. Another possibility: kernel auto-selector is switching between q4k and fp16 mid-rollout when KV cache hit rates change; the transition path can deopt and force re-warm of caches. Need trace-level profile to confirm.

Priya (eng-runtime): Can we get the customer to temporarily 1) route traffic back to FP16 or 2) pin the endpoint to force FP16 kernels? Command to route: `rwdctl route set acme-prod-gen --model redwood/open-oz-7b-fp16`

Sam (customer-success): Customer agreed to a temporary fallback. I'll flip routing to FP16 and report back with p95 in 15m.

ops-bot: Deploy / routing change applied by sam - change-id=chg-9821 at 2026-11-04T17:20:03Z

Sam (customer-success): after rollback to FP16: p95 ~= 190ms (back to baseline). Customer confirms reduced hallucinations in their test set.

Marta (eng-ml): please collect a perf profile for a failing quant request so we can reproduce on staging. Run:

```
rwd profile --req abc123 --trace /tmp/abc123.trace.json
nvidia-smi dmon -s u -o DT > /tmp/gpu-dmon.log &
# also capture rwd runtime logs with DEBUG=runtime
```

Priya (eng-runtime): created internal ticket INFR-2345 with tags: kernel-routing, calib-cache, kvcache. Plan: repro on staging, add stricter calibration-cache keying (include quant config), and guard training/auto-select transitions to avoid mid-request kernel flips.

Sam (customer-success): cc acme-platform — we're on it. I'll update customer thread with ETA and temporary mitigation.

acme-platform: thanks for the fast response. We'll keep traffic pinned to FP16 until you confirm a safe fix. :+1:

Marta (eng-ml): next steps for us: reproduce, minimal patch to calibration cache keying, add unit test, lock kernel-selection during active KV-cache warmup windows. Prioritize for next patch release.

Priya (eng-runtime): assigning to eng-runtime and eng-ml owners in INFR-2345. Sam — please attach all customer traces and one failing prompt to the ticket.

Sam (customer-success): will attach traces. Will follow up with customer status update in 30m. Thanks all. :pray:
